meta.title: DTerm — connect, authenticate, attach, come back

views.label: Proving the secret
views.note: The order is fixed and the whole exchange gets five seconds.

views.label: Finding the shell
views.note: The session is connected to if it exists, and spawned only if it does not.

views.label: Losing the phone
views.note: The connection dies, the shell keeps running, and the scrollback fills the screen back in.

messages.label: fork one process for this client
AUTH  HMAC-SHA256(secret, challenge)
messages.note: The secret itself never travels, and the next challenge differs

messages.label: connect to the Unix socket
messages.note: Spawns the session only when no socket answers

messages.label: forkpty  bash --login
messages.note: Nothing here runs until the secret is proven

messages.label: OUTPUT frames
messages.note: The connection process only copies bytes; it parses nothing after AUTH

messages.label: the phone goes away
messages.note: The connection process exits; the session sets its client to -1 and never signals the shell

messages.label: keeps working
messages.note: Read even with nobody attached, or the buffer fills and bash blocks

cards.title: Nothing is spawned on trust
items: HELLO, CHALLENGE, AUTH, AUTH_OK and ATTACH must arrive in that order
Anything else in between drops the connection, and the whole exchange gets five seconds
forkpty runs after AUTH_OK, so a wrong secret never costs a shell

cards.title: Attach, do not create
items: ATTACH names a session; an empty name means default
A live socket is connected to, a stale one is unlinked and replaced
A second client taking over closes the first rather than sharing

cards.title: Coming back is cheap
items: Losing the phone only closes a socket in the session process
The shell keeps its working directory, environment and running jobs
The replayed scrollback is what makes reattaching look instant
